entries.x: What meilisearch-cdc is, how snapshot-then-stream change data capture into Meilisearch works, the core concepts and the feature overview. meilisearch-cdc copies a table once, then streams every insert, update and delete into a Meilisearch index in near real time. It ships as one self-contained program with an embedded state store and a live dashboard, and it starts with zero configuration. The overview page: every pipeline, its throughput and the health of each Meilisearch instance, updated live.

meilisearch-cdc is a change data capture (CDC) service for Meilisearch. You connect a database (or a stream, or your own application over HTTP), pick a table, and describe how rows become documents. The service then keeps a Meilisearch index in step with that table: it copies the existing rows once (the snapshot), then follows the database's change log and applies each change. One binary, one data directory. State (tasks, checkpoints, users, alert history) lives in an embedded bbolt database, cdc.db, in the data directory. Writes go through the official meilisearch-go SDK. Everything is managed in the dashboard: sources, Meilisearch destinations, sync tasks, users, alerts and AI access. The same operations are available in the REST API, to AI agents over MCP, and on the server through the admin CLI.

Each task runs a small pipeline: Open and validate. The source connects and checks the server's prerequisites (for example wal_level=logical on PostgreSQL or binlog_format=ROW on MySQL). Problems that retrying cannot fix fail the task with a message that says what to change. Capture the position, then snapshot. The current source position (an LSN, binlog coordinates, a resume token…) is recorded before the copy starts, then every existing row is read in chunks and written to Meilisearch. Stream. When the snapshot is done, streaming starts from the position captured before it, so changes made during the copy are replayed and nothing falls into a gap. Checkpoint after confirmation. A position is saved only after Meilisearch confirms the batch that contains it. A crash, even kill -9, replays from the last checkpoint.

Because the checkpoint trails the confirmed writes, some changes can be delivered twice after a restart. That is harmless: each document is addressed by its primary key, so writing the same row again leaves the index in the same state. Changes to the same document inside one batch are coalesced, so only the final state is sent.

Transient errors (network, Meilisearch 5xx or 429, a full task queue) are retried with exponential backoff and jitter. If the pipeline itself fails, a supervisor restarts it with a backoff from 1 s up to 1 minute and the task shows retrying. A payload that is too large is split in two and retried. Documents Meilisearch rejects (an invalid id, a malformed _geo or vector…) are isolated by bisecting the batch; the rest is applied and the offenders go to the dead letter queue. A lost source position (a purged binlog, a dropped replication slot, an expired stream shard) triggers an automatic full resync. Safety guards hold the task (state held) instead of deleting a large share of the index or applying a TRUNCATE, until an operator decides. See safety guards.

Concept What it is Connector A saved source connection: the source type and its credentials, encrypted at rest. It can be tested, and its tables, collections, topics or streams can be browsed. Many tasks can reuse one connector. See Sources and connectors. Destination A named Meilisearch instance: URL, API key, gzip, request timeout and a background health check every 5 s to 1 h. Its health, the tasks writing to it and the last sync time update live. See Destinations. Task Connector + table → destination + index. A task defines the column mapping, the index settings, batching, retries and safety guards. One table can feed several instances through several tasks. See Create a task. Index The Meilisearch index a task writes to. The task creates it on first write with its primary key field, can manage its settings and reports drift. See Index management. Checkpoint The last source position confirmed in Meilisearch, plus the position captured before the snapshot. Resetting it makes the next start copy everything again.

11 kinds of sourcesPostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, DynamoDB, CouchDB, SQL Server, CockroachDB, Kafka (Debezium), Redis Streams, SQL polling and an HTTP webhook. Many Meilisearch instancesAny number of destinations, health checked in the background, or a single instance pinned with MEILI_URL. MappingInclude, exclude and rename columns, composite keys, soft deletes, _geo, time formats and static fields. Index managementEvery Meilisearch setting, drift detection, one-click apply, swap, compaction, search playground and documents browser. Zero-downtime resyncRebuild into a shadow index and swap it in, so search never goes empty. Data qualitySchema check, document-level diff with repair, and a dead letter queue with replay and discard. AlertsTask state, lag, dead letters, error bursts, stalled snapshots and Meilisearch down, by email, Telegram or webhook. Team and securityViewer, moderator and admin roles, invitations, sessions with CSRF protection, audit log, AES-256-GCM secrets. AI agentsA Model Context Protocol server with role-scoped tokens, so assistants can inspect and operate pipelines. ObservabilityPrometheus metrics, a live dashboard over Server-Sent Events, structured logs and optional pprof. Operator CLIRecover accounts, transfer ownership, sign everyone out and purge stored data from the server. GitOpsDeclare tasks in a YAML file applied at startup, and import or export tasks as JSON.

Download meilisearch-cdc, verify the checksum, start it, create the admin account and sync your first table into Meilisearch in five minutes. Download one binary, start it, create the admin account in the browser and follow the onboarding flow: a Meilisearch destination, a connector, then your first sync task. Just want to see it run? The Docker Compose demo starts Meilisearch, PostgreSQL with 10,000 products and a running sync in one command.

A reachable Meilisearch instance and an API key that can write documents and manage indexes (the master key or an admin key works; see API key permissions). A source prepared for change data capture. For PostgreSQL that means wal_level=logical; every source page lists its prerequisites, for example PostgreSQL or MySQL.

Every GitHub release ships one archive per platform plus a checksums.txt file. Archive names follow meilisearch-cdc_<version>_<os>_<arch>, where the version has no leading v: Platform Archive Linux x86-64 meilisearch-cdc_<version>_linux_amd64.tar.gz Linux ARM64 meilisearch-cdc_<version>_linux_arm64.tar.gz macOS Intel meilisearch-cdc_<version>_darwin_amd64.tar.gz macOS Apple silicon meilisearch-cdc_<version>_darwin_arm64.tar.gz Windows x86-64 meilisearch-cdc_<version>_windows_amd64.zip Windows ARM64 meilisearch-cdc_<version>_windows_arm64.zip Each archive contains a folder of the same name with the meilisearch-cdc binary (meilisearch-cdc.exe on Windows), README.md and docs/api.md and docs/cli.md. The binaries are static (built without cgo) and need nothing else. # Linux or macOS: pick the version and platform you need. VERSION=1.2.3 # the release tag without the leading "v" OS=linux ARCH=amd64 # darwin / arm64 on Apple silicon NAME=meilisearch-cdc_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH} curl -LO https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc/releases/download/v${VERSION}/${NAME}.tar.gz curl -LO https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc/releases/download/v${VERSION}/checksums.txt

checksums.txt holds the SHA-256 of every archive, in the format of sha256sum. # Linux: prints "<archive>: OK" grep " ${NAME}.tar.gz\$" checksums.txt | sha256sum --check # macOS grep " ${NAME}.tar.gz\$" checksums.txt | shasum -a 256 --check # Windows PowerShell $name = "meilisearch-cdc_1.2.3_windows_amd64.zip" $expected = (Select-String -Path checksums.txt -Pattern $name).Line.Split(" ")[0] $actual = (Get-FileHash $name -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() if ($actual -eq $expected) { "OK" } else { "MISMATCH" } Then unpack it: tar -xzf ${NAME}.tar.gz cd ${NAME} ./meilisearch-cdc version Expand-Archive meilisearch-cdc_1.2.3_windows_amd64.zip -DestinationPath . .\meilisearch-cdc_1.2.3_windows_amd64\meilisearch-cdc.exe version meilisearch-cdc version prints the release tag it was built from (a build from source prints dev).

No configuration is required. Without flags the service listens on :8080 and keeps its state in ./data: ./meilisearch-cdc # or choose the address and the data directory: ./meilisearch-cdc -listen 127.0.0.1:8080 -data-dir /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc On the first start the service creates the data directory (mode 0700), the state database cdc.db and a random encryption key in secret.key (mode 0600). Until an account exists it logs: level=WARN msg="no user exists yet: open the dashboard to create the first admin (or set CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL and CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD)" level=INFO msg=listening addr=:8080 meilisearch="" Back up secret.key with the data Connector passwords and Meilisearch API keys are encrypted with this key. Losing it means re-entering every credential. See Backups and upgrades.

Open http://localhost:8080. While no account exists, the dashboard shows the setup page: enter an email, a name and a password of 8 to 128 characters. This first account is an admin and the primary administrator of the installation. To skip the setup page (for automated deployments), set CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL and CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD (or CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE) before the first start: the account is created when no user exists yet.

After the first sign-in the dashboard opens an onboarding flow with three steps. Each step can be skipped and done later from the menu. Add a destination. Name your Meilisearch instance, enter its URL (for example http://localhost:7700) and API key, and test the connection. The first destination becomes the default one. Details: Destinations. Add a connector. Choose the source type, enter the connection string and test it: the test reports the server version and the tables it can see. Details: Connectors. Create the first task. The wizard asks for the table, the mapping, the index and the sync options. Test connection shows the columns and five transformed sample documents before you save. Details: Create a task. The wizard tests the connection and previews transformed documents before anything is written. Start the task. It moves through starting and snapshotting (with a progress bar) to streaming. Change a row in the source and watch the document change in the index's search tab a moment later.

Images are published to the GitHub Container Registry for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64: docker run -d --name cdc -p 8080:8080 -v cdc-data:/data ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:latest The image stores its state in the /data volume and runs as a non-root user. See Docker and Compose for tags, environment variables and secrets.

The repository's deploy/docker-compose.yml starts Meilisearch, PostgreSQL 17 (with wal_level=logical and 10,000 seeded products) and meilisearch-cdc built from the source tree, with a declarative task already running: git clone https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc.git cd meilisearch-cdc docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build Open http://localhost:8080 and sign in as admin@example.com with the password change-me-please. Meilisearch listens on http://localhost:7700 with the master key masterKey. The demo pins the service to that Meilisearch with MEILI_URL (single-instance mode) and applies deploy/tasks.yaml at startup (declarative tasks). Demo values only The demo's passwords and keys are public. Do not reuse that file for a real deployment.
Install it as a service with a dedicated user and data directory. Put it behind TLS before exposing the dashboard. Invite your team with the right roles, and set up alerts.

Install the meilisearch-cdc binary on Linux (systemd), macOS (launchd) or Windows (service or terminal) with a dedicated user and data directory. meilisearch-cdc is one static binary. Install it, give it a data directory that only its own user can read, and let your init system keep it running.

A data directory (CDC_DATA_DIR, default ./data). It holds cdc.db (the state database), secret.key (unless you set CDC_SECRET_KEY) and, while the service runs, the admin socket admin.sock. The service creates it with mode 0700. One HTTP port (CDC_LISTEN, default :8080) for the dashboard, the REST API, /metrics and /mcp. Outbound access to your sources and Meilisearch instances. A single instance per data directory. The state database is locked by the running process, so run exactly one replica per data directory. Download and verify the archive for your platform as described in the quick start. All settings are optional; see the configuration reference.

entries.h: Install the binary and create a user
entries.x: VERSION=1.2.3 ARCH=amd64 NAME=meilisearch-cdc_${VERSION}_linux_${ARCH} tar -xzf ${NAME}.tar.gz sudo install -m 0755 ${NAME}/meilisearch-cdc /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc # A system user without a login shell, and its data directory. sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc --shell /usr/sbin/nologin meilisearch-cdc sudo install -d -o meilisearch-cdc -g meilisearch-cdc -m 0700 /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc sudo install -d -o root -g meilisearch-cdc -m 0750 /etc/meilisearch-cdc

Keep settings in an environment file readable only by root and the service group: # /etc/meilisearch-cdc/cdc.env (chmod 0640, owner root:meilisearch-cdc) CDC_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/meilisearch-cdc CDC_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8080 CDC_LOG_FORMAT=json # Behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (see the reverse proxy page): CDC_PUBLIC_URL=https://cdc.example.com CDC_TRUST_PROXY=true CDC_COOKIE_SECURE=true Secrets can be kept out of the environment with the *_FILE variants, for example CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/etc/meilisearch-cdc/secret-key. See Secrets and *_FILE.

# /etc/systemd/system/meilisearch-cdc.service [Unit] Description=meilisearch-cdc: change data capture into Meilisearch Documentation=https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/ Wants=network-online.target After=network-online.target [Service] User=meilisearch-cdc Group=meilisearch-cdc EnvironmentFile=/etc/meilisearch-cdc/cdc.env ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc Restart=on-failure RestartSec=5 # SIGTERM drains running tasks for CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT (20s), then the # service allows 10 more seconds to shut down: keep this above the sum. TimeoutStopSec=45 UMask=0077 NoNewPrivileges=true ProtectSystem=strict ProtectHome=true PrivateTmp=true ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/meilisearch-cdc [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now meilisearch-cdc sudo systemctl status meilisearch-cdc journalctl -u meilisearch-cdc -f The service stops cleanly on SIGTERM or SIGINT: running tasks flush and confirm pending batches for up to CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT, and anything unconfirmed is replayed from the checkpoint on the next start.

entries.h: Using the admin CLI on the server
entries.x: Run the admin CLI as the service user with the same environment, so it finds the same data directory and key: sudo -u meilisearch-cdc env $(sudo grep -v '^#' /etc/meilisearch-cdc/cdc.env | xargs) \ meilisearch-cdc admin users list

There is no Homebrew formula; install the release binary and run it with launchd. Use darwin_arm64 on Apple silicon and darwin_amd64 on Intel Macs. VERSION=1.2.3 ARCH=arm64 NAME=meilisearch-cdc_${VERSION}_darwin_${ARCH} tar -xzf ${NAME}.tar.gz sudo install -m 0755 ${NAME}/meilisearch-cdc /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc # Downloaded with a browser? Remove the quarantine flag: sudo xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc 2>/dev/null || true mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/Application Support/meilisearch-cdc" "$HOME/Library/Logs" A per-user launch agent that starts at login and restarts on failure: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!-- ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc.plist --> <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd"> <plist version="1.0"> <dict> <key>Label</key><string>com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc</string> <key>ProgramArguments</key> <array><string>/usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc</string></array> <key>EnvironmentVariables</key> <dict> <key>CDC_DATA_DIR</key><string>/Users/you/Library/Application Support/meilisearch-cdc</string> <key>CDC_LISTEN</key><string>127.0.0.1:8080</string> </dict> <key>RunAtLoad</key><true/> <key>KeepAlive</key><dict><key>SuccessfulExit</key><false/></dict> <key>ExitTimeOut</key><integer>45</integer> <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/you/Library/Logs/meilisearch-cdc.log</string> <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/you/Library/Logs/meilisearch-cdc.log</string> </dict> </plist> launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc.plist launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc # restart launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc # stop and unload Keep the data directory path short The admin socket lives at <data-dir>/admin.sock, and Unix socket paths are limited to about 100 characters. With a longer path the service logs a warning and runs without the socket. In our tests on macOS the CLI then also failed while the service was stopped (connect: invalid argument), so prefer a short absolute path such as /usr/local/var/meilisearch-cdc, or run the CLI from inside the data directory with CDC_DATA_DIR=..

Unzip the archive and run meilisearch-cdc.exe from a terminal. The data directory defaults to .\data next to where you start it, so set it explicitly: $env:CDC_DATA_DIR = "C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc" $env:CDC_LISTEN = "127.0.0.1:8080" & "C:\Program Files\meilisearch-cdc\meilisearch-cdc.exe"

The binary does not implement the Windows Service Control Manager protocol, so sc.exe create alone would time out when starting it (error 1053). Use a service wrapper such as NSSM, which starts the executable and stops it on service shutdown: nssm install meilisearch-cdc "C:\Program Files\meilisearch-cdc\meilisearch-cdc.exe" nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppEnvironmentExtra CDC_DATA_DIR=C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc CDC_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8080 nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppStdout C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc\service.log nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppStderr C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc\service.log nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppStopMethodConsole 45000 nssm start meilisearch-cdc Restrict C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc to the service account and administrators: it contains the encryption key. On Windows the admin CLI has no hidden password prompt; use --generate or --password-file.

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz # ok curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/health # {"meilisearch":{"error":"no Meilisearch destination is configured: add one first","status":"unconfigured"},"status":"ok"} /healthz answers ok as long as the process serves HTTP, which suits liveness probes. /api/v1/health also reports the default Meilisearch destination. Both need no authentication.

Run meilisearch-cdc in Docker: image tags, the /data volume, the non-root user, environment variables, secrets files and the Compose demo stack. The official image is small (a distroless base with only the static binary), runs as a non-root user and keeps all state in the /data volume.

Images are published to ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 on every release tag: Tag Points to 1.2.3 That exact release (the Git tag v1.2.3). 1.2 The newest release of the 1.2 line. latest The newest final release. Pre-releases such as v1.3.0-rc.1 get their version tag but never latest. Pin an exact version in production and upgrade on purpose (see Upgrading).

Setting Value Base gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot (no shell, no package manager) Binary /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc (the entrypoint) User nonroot:nonroot (uid and gid 65532 in distroless images) Environment CDC_LISTEN=:8080, CDC_DATA_DIR=/data Volume /data Port 8080

docker volume create cdc-data docker run -d --name cdc --restart unless-stopped \ -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 \ -v cdc-data:/data \ -e CDC_PUBLIC_URL=https://cdc.example.com \ ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3 docker logs -f cdc Open the dashboard and create the admin account (or pass CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL and CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD). Flags work too, since the binary is the entrypoint: docker run … ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3 -log-format json. Bind mounts and the non-root user A named volume is initialised with the right owner. With a bind mount (-v /srv/cdc:/data) the host directory must be writable by uid 65532: sudo install -d -o 65532 -g 65532 -m 0700 /srv/cdc. Otherwise the service cannot create cdc.db and exits.

Every secret setting also reads a file named by <NAME>_FILE, which matches Docker and Kubernetes secrets. Trailing newlines are removed. printf '%s' "$(openssl rand -base64 32)" > cdc-secret-key docker run -d --name cdc -p 8080:8080 -v cdc-data:/data \ -v "$PWD/cdc-secret-key:/run/secrets/cdc-key:ro" \ -e CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/cdc-key \ ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3 Supported: CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE, CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS_FILE, MEILI_API_KEY_FILE, CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE, CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE. When the file cannot be read, the plain variable is used instead.

entries.h: The admin CLI inside the container
entries.x: The image has no shell, but the binary runs fine with docker exec. It inherits the container's environment, so it finds /data and the key: docker exec -it cdc meilisearch-cdc admin users list docker exec -it cdc meilisearch-cdc admin users reset-password --email you@example.com --generate

A production-style Compose file with Meilisearch and secrets kept in files: services: meilisearch: image: getmeili/meilisearch:latest # pin the version you run environment: MEILI_MASTER_KEY: ${MEILI_MASTER_KEY} # from an .env file next to this one MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS: "true" volumes: [meili:/meili_data] cdc: image: ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3 restart: unless-stopped depends_on: [meilisearch] ports: ["127.0.0.1:8080:8080"] environment: CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/cdc_secret_key CDC_PUBLIC_URL: https://cdc.example.com CDC_TRUST_PROXY: "true" CDC_COOKIE_SECURE: "true" CDC_LOG_FORMAT: json GOMEMLIMIT: 400MiB # about 80% of the memory limit volumes: [cdc:/data] secrets: [cdc_secret_key] deploy: resources: limits: {memory: 512M} secrets: cdc_secret_key: {file: ./secrets/cdc_secret_key} volumes: {meili: {}, cdc: {}} Add the Meilisearch destination in the dashboard (URL http://meilisearch:7700), or pin the service to it with MEILI_URL and MEILI_API_KEY_FILE (single-instance mode).

The repository's deploy/docker-compose.yml builds the service from source and starts it next to Meilisearch and PostgreSQL 17 with a seeded products table: docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build # or: make demo Service Port Notes meilisearch 7700 master key masterKey postgres 5432 wal_level=logical; user, password and database shop; seeded by deploy/seed.sql cdc 8080 admin admin@example.com / change-me-please, MEILI_URL set, CDC_TASKS_FILE=/etc/cdc/tasks.yaml The task in deploy/tasks.yaml syncs products with soft deletes on deleted_at, Unix timestamps, a _geo field and managed index settings; it is shown in full on the declarative tasks page. Remove everything with docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml down -v.

docker build -t meilisearch-cdc --build-arg VERSION=v1.2.3 . # or: make docker The Dockerfile cross-compiles in the build stage (golang:1.27.3-alpine, CGO_ENABLED=0), so multi-architecture builds need no emulation: docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 ….

Deploy meilisearch-cdc on Kubernetes with a single-replica Deployment, a PersistentVolumeClaim and Secrets mounted through the *_FILE variables. Run meilisearch-cdc as a single-replica Deployment with a persistent volume for its embedded state store, and pass secrets as files. Exactly one replica All state (tasks, checkpoints, users) lives in one embedded database file that a single process locks. Do not scale the Deployment above one replica, and use the Recreate strategy so the old pod releases the volume before the new one starts. For more throughput, raise the per-task batching settings or run separate installations with separate data directories.

Generate an encryption key once and keep it outside the cluster as well: without it, stored credentials cannot be decrypted. kubectl create namespace cdc kubectl -n cdc create secret generic meilisearch-cdc \ --from-literal=secret-key="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" \ --from-literal=admin-token="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \ --from-literal=admin-password='choose-a-strong-password' A base64 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes is used as the AES-256 key directly; any other value is treated as a passphrase and stretched with argon2id.

Probes. /healthz needs no authentication and answers ok while the HTTP server runs. Do not use /api/v1/health as a liveness probe: it also checks Meilisearch, and a Meilisearch outage should not restart this pod. Admin account. CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL with CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE creates the first admin on start when no user exists; afterwards they are ignored. Metrics. /metrics requires authentication. Give Prometheus the admin token as a bearer token; see Prometheus. Admin CLI. kubectl -n cdc exec -it deploy/meilisearch-cdc -- meilisearch-cdc admin users list talks to the running service over its socket in /data. Declarative tasks. Mount a ConfigMap with a tasks file and set CDC_TASKS_FILE; credentials come from environment variables expanded with ${VAR}. See Declarative tasks file. Server-Sent Events. If an Ingress controller buffers responses, the dashboard's live updates stall. For ingress-nginx, set the annotations nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffering: "off" and a long proxy-read-timeout. See Reverse proxy and TLS.
Snapshot the volume while the pod is scaled to zero, or copy /data/cdc.db as described in Backups and upgrades. The key lives in the Secret, so back that up too.

Put meilisearch-cdc behind nginx or Caddy with TLS: Server-Sent Events settings, CDC_TRUST_PROXY, CDC_COOKIE_SECURE and CDC_PUBLIC_URL. meilisearch-cdc serves plain HTTP. Put a TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of it, keep Server-Sent Events unbuffered, and tell the service it sits behind a proxy.

Variable Why CDC_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8080 Only the proxy reaches the service. CDC_TRUST_PROXY=true Uses X-Forwarded-For (first address) as the client IP for login rate limiting and the audit log, and X-Forwarded-Proto: https to mark the session cookie Secure. Enable it only when every request comes through a proxy that sets these headers, otherwise clients can spoof their IP. CDC_COOKIE_SECURE=true Always sets the Secure flag on the cdc_session cookie, whatever the headers say. CDC_PUBLIC_URL=https://cdc.example.com The base URL in emailed links (invitations, password resets, alert emails). It can also be set in Settings → Email; without either, the request's origin is used. Keep the Host header Cookie-authenticated writes are protected against CSRF by comparing the browser's Origin (or Referer) host with the request's Host. Forward the original Host header, or every save in the dashboard fails with 403 cross-origin request refused.

/api/v1/events is a Server-Sent Events stream that stays open. The service already sends X-Accel-Buffering: no and Cache-Control: no-cache; the proxy must not buffer it and must allow long reads. /api/v1/ingest/{task} (the webhook source) answers only after Meilisearch confirmed the documents, up to 60 seconds, and accepts bodies up to 64 MiB. /mcp is the MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP), which may also stream responses.

server { listen 443 ssl; http2 on; server_name cdc.example.com; ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/cdc.example.com/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/cdc.example.com/privkey.pem; client_max_body_size 64m; # webhook ingest bodies location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_read_timeout 120s; } # Live dashboard updates (Server-Sent Events) and MCP streams. location ~ ^/(api/v1/events|mcp)$ { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_read_timeout 1h; } } server { listen 80; server_name cdc.example.com; return 301 https://$host$request_uri; } With proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for, a client-supplied header is kept in front of the real address. If nginx is the only entry point, prefer proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; so the first address is always the one nginx saw.

Caddy obtains certificates automatically, sets X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto, forwards the Host header and flushes Server-Sent Events immediately: cdc.example.com { request_body { max_size 64MB } reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 { flush_interval -1 } }
The dashboard calls the API at /api/v1 and the service worker registers at the root, so serve meilisearch-cdc on its own host name (cdc.example.com) rather than under a path such as example.com/cdc/.

The dashboard shows Live in the top bar (SSE works through the proxy). The session cookie is Secure (browser developer tools → Application → Cookies). Invitation and reset emails link to https://cdc.example.com. The audit log shows real client IPs, not the proxy's. The browser offers to install the app (installing needs HTTPS; see Mobile and app install).

Back up the meilisearch-cdc data directory and secret key, restore it, and upgrade the binary or the Docker image safely. Everything meilisearch-cdc knows lives in its data directory. Back up cdc.db and the encryption key together, and you can rebuild the installation anywhere.

Item Where Contains cdc.db $CDC_DATA_DIR/cdc.db Tasks, connectors, destinations, checkpoints, task statuses, dead letters, diff reports, users, sessions, invitations, alert rules and history, MCP tokens and policy, SMTP and Telegram settings, the audit log. Credentials inside it are encrypted. The encryption key $CDC_DATA_DIR/secret.key, or wherever CDC_SECRET_KEY / CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE comes from The key that decrypts connector passwords, DynamoDB secret keys, Meilisearch API keys, the SMTP password and the Telegram bot token. Your configuration Environment file, unit file, Compose file, tasks file How the service is started. The task activity log is kept in memory only and is not part of a backup. The documents themselves live in Meilisearch; back them up there (dumps and snapshots can be requested from the destination's Backups tab). Without the key, credentials are lost A backup of cdc.db without its key still restores tasks, users and history, but every stored secret fails to decrypt (cannot decrypt secret: wrong key or the value belongs to another record) and must be entered again. Store the key separately from the database backup, for example in your secret manager.

The database is a single bbolt file that the running service keeps open. The simplest consistent backup is a cold copy: sudo systemctl stop meilisearch-cdc sudo tar -C /var/lib -czf /backup/meilisearch-cdc-$(date +%F).tar.gz meilisearch-cdc sudo systemctl start meilisearch-cdc Stopping is safe: tasks drain and save their checkpoint, and resume where they stopped. Changes made in the source meanwhile stay in the source's log (replication slot, binlog, change stream…) as long as its retention allows. With Docker, stop the container and archive the volume: docker stop cdc docker run --rm -v cdc-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \ tar -C /data -czf /backup/cdc-data-$(date +%F).tar.gz . docker start cdc If you take filesystem or volume snapshots instead (LVM, ZFS, EBS, Kubernetes VolumeSnapshots), make them crash-consistent: bbolt is designed to survive a crash, so an atomic snapshot of the whole volume is a valid backup. Copying the file with cp while the service writes to it is not.

Stop the service and replace the data directory with the backup (owner and mode as before: the service user, 0700). Provide the same key: the restored secret.key, or the same CDC_SECRET_KEY. Start the service. Tasks whose desired state is running start again from their checkpoints. A restored checkpoint may point to a source position that no longer exists (the binlog was purged, the replication slot was dropped, the stream was trimmed). The task then logs source position lost and runs a full resync automatically. If you restore onto a different source database, use Reset checkpoint on the affected tasks so they snapshot again.

Read the release notes of every version you skip (Changelog and upgrade notes). Take a backup as above. Replace the binary (or change the image tag) and restart. On start the service opens the existing database, re-encrypts any secret still stored with an older key or format, and resumes tasks from their checkpoints. Reload the dashboard. Installed apps pick up the new version through the service worker and offer Reload (see updates). # Binary sudo install -m 0755 meilisearch-cdc_1.2.4_linux_amd64/meilisearch-cdc /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc sudo systemctl restart meilisearch-cdc # Docker docker pull ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.4 docker rm -f cdc && docker run -d --name cdc -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -v cdc-data:/data ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.4 To roll back, stop the service and restore the backup taken before the upgrade together with the older binary.

To wipe the stored data but keep the installation (and its key), use meilisearch-cdc admin purge all; see Admin CLI. Purging does not touch Meilisearch indexes unless you purge tasks with --indexes, and does not drop replication slots in your databases.

Every meilisearch-cdc flag and environment variable with its default, the *_FILE secret variants, single-instance mode, logging, pprof and metrics. Every setting is optional: with none, the service listens on :8080, stores its state in ./data and is configured in the dashboard. Settings come from environment variables and command-line flags; a flag wins over its variable.

Environment variable Flag Default Description CDC_LISTEN -listen :8080 HTTP listen address for the dashboard, API, /metrics and /mcp. CDC_DATA_DIR -data-dir ./data Directory of the state database cdc.db, the generated secret.key and the admin socket admin.sock. Created with mode 0700. CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN -admin-token empty Static bearer token with the admin role, for scripts, Prometheus and webhook pushers (details). Only its hash is kept in memory. Secret: also CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE. CDC_SECRET_KEY -secret-key generated in secret.key Key that encrypts stored credentials: a base64 string of exactly 32 bytes is used as the AES-256 key, anything else is a passphrase stretched with argon2id. Secret: also CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE. CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS none empty An older key that can still decrypt; used for key rotation. Secret: also CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS_FILE. CDC_COOKIE_SECURE -cookie-secure false Always set the Secure flag on the session cookie (behind a TLS-terminating proxy). Five settings are secrets. Each can be read from a file whose path is in <NAME>_FILE, which is how Docker and Kubernetes mount secrets. Trailing \r and \n are removed. When the variable <NAME>_FILE is set and the file is readable, it wins over <NAME>. Secret File variant CDC_SECRET_KEY CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS_FILE MEILI_API_KEY MEILI_API_KEY_FILE CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE MEILI_MASTER_KEY (the fallback for MEILI_API_KEY) has no file variant. Credentials you enter in the dashboard (connector passwords, DynamoDB secret keys, Meilisearch API keys, the SMTP password, the Telegram bot token) are stored encrypted in cdc.db with AES-256-GCM and never returned by the API. See Secrets encryption.

entries.h: Single-instance mode vs. destinations in the dashboard
entries.x: meilisearch-cdc can write to many Meilisearch instances (destinations). How they are managed depends on MEILI_URL: MEILI_URL unset (default) MEILI_URL set Destinations Created, edited and deleted in the dashboard or the API. The first one becomes the default. One destination with the id default, marked managedByEnv. Its URL and key come from the environment and are refreshed at every start. Other stored destinations Visible and usable. Hidden. Creating, deleting or switching destinations Allowed (admin). Refused with 409: single instance mode: MEILI_URL is set, so the service writes only to that Meilisearch instance; unset it to manage destinations in the dashboard. Dashboard Destinations page with add/edit. GET /api/v1/auth/config reports "singleDestination": true and the UI hides destination management. The service logs single instance mode: writing only to MEILI_URL at startup. To switch back to managed destinations, unset MEILI_URL and restart; the destinations stored earlier reappear.

Logs are structured (Go log/slog) and written to standard error. Every line carries the version attribute. time=2026-10-26T23:41:57.571+03:30 level=INFO msg=listening version=v1.2.3 addr=127.0.0.1:8080 meilisearch="" With CDC_LOG_FORMAT=json each line is a JSON object, convenient for Loki, Elasticsearch or CloudWatch. Per-task activity (snapshot started, streaming from a position, retries, holds) is also kept in memory, the last 1,000 entries per task, and shown on the task's Logs tab and streamed live.

With CDC_PPROF=true the Go profiler is served at /debug/pprof/ (index, profile, trace, symbol, cmdline). It requires authentication like the API: a session cookie or the admin token. curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN" -o cpu.pprof \ "http://127.0.0.1:8080/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30" go tool pprof -http=:0 cpu.pprof Who can read profiles The flag's help text says "admins", but the route is registered as a read (GET) route, and reads are allowed to every signed-in role, viewers included. Enable pprof only while you need it.
Prometheus metrics are always served at /metrics and need authentication. The metric names and labels are listed under Monitoring.

Variable Effect GOMEMLIMIT Go runtime soft memory limit, e.g. 400MiB. Set it to about 80% of a container's memory limit. See Performance. GOGC Garbage collector target (default 100). Higher values trade memory for less GC CPU. AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_PROFILE, … Used by DynamoDB connectors that leave the region or keys empty (the default AWS credential chain). Any variable named in a tasks file Expanded as ${VAR} in CDC_TASKS_FILE.

Define meilisearch-cdc sync tasks in a YAML or JSON file applied at startup (CDC_TASKS_FILE), with ${VAR} expansion for credentials. Keep sync tasks in Git: list them in a YAML or JSON file, point CDC_TASKS_FILE (or -tasks) at it, and the service creates or updates them every time it starts.

The file is read once at startup, after stored tasks are resumed. Before parsing, every ${VAR} (or $VAR) is replaced with the environment variable of that name, so credentials stay out of the file. An unset variable becomes an empty string. Expansion happens on the whole file, so a literal $ written in the file (inside a password, say) is expanded too: keep such values in environment variables. Every task needs an id (letters, digits, - and _, at most 64 characters). It is the key that matches a task in the file to a stored task. A task with a new id is created; it starts right away when desiredState: running. A task whose id exists is updated with the file's definition (a running task restarts). Then its desiredState is applied: running starts it, stopped or paused stops it, and an omitted value leaves it as it is. If the source table, schema, database, connector or the index uid or destination changed, the checkpoint is cleared and the next start runs a full snapshot. Tasks that are not in the file are left alone; removing a task from the file does not delete it. Any error (unreadable file, invalid YAML, a missing id, a validation error) stops the startup: the service logs stopped with error with the reason (for example task products: name is required) and exits with status 1. Tasks created from the file are ordinary tasks: they appear in the dashboard and can be operated there. Edits made in the dashboard are overwritten by the file at the next start.

The file has a single top-level key, tasks, holding a list of task definitions. The fields are the JSON fields of a task, described on Create a task; YAML and JSON are both accepted (JSON is valid YAML). Durations are strings like 500ms or 2s.

# Declarative tasks, applied at startup (created or updated by id). # ${VAR} is expanded from the environment, so secrets stay out of this file. tasks: - id: products name: Postgres products desiredState: running source: type: postgres dsn: ${PG_DSN} table: products mapping: softDeleteColumn: deleted_at timeFormat: unix geo: {lat: lat, lng: lng} index: uid: products manageSettings: true settings: searchableAttributes: [name, description, category] filterableAttributes: [category, price, in_stock, _geo, updated_at] sortableAttributes: [price, updated_at, _geo] typoTolerance: {enabled: true} sync: batchSize: 5000 flushInterval: 500ms maxInflight: 8 safety: maxDeleteRatio: 0.3 zeroDowntimeResync: true The Compose demo sets PG_DSN=postgres://shop:shop@postgres:5432/shop?sslmode=disable and CDC_TASKS_FILE=/etc/cdc/tasks.yaml, and mounts the file read-only.

Two tasks: one using an inline connection, one reusing a connector created in the dashboard (its id is shown on the connector page), writing to a named destination. tasks: - id: orders-search name: MySQL orders description: Orders searchable by customer and status tags: [shop, mysql] desiredState: running source: type: mysql dsn: ${ORDERS_DSN} # cdc:secret@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop table: orders serverId: 4242 # unique among the server's replicas mapping: primaryKey: [id] exclude: [internal_notes] rename: {customer_email: email} static: {tenant: acme} timeFormat: unix index: uid: orders writeMode: replace manageSettings: true settings: filterableAttributes: [status, tenant, created_at] sortableAttributes: [created_at] sync: mode: snapshot_stream batchSize: 2000 flushInterval: 1s maxInflight: 4 retry: {maxAttempts: 8, initialBackoff: 200ms, maxBackoff: 30s} safety: maxDeleteRatio: 0.2 minDocsForDeleteGuard: 1000 allowTruncate: false zeroDowntimeResync: true dumpBeforeResync: false - id: catalog-eu name: Catalog to the EU instance desiredState: running source: connectorId: pg-catalog # a saved connector schema: public table: products index: uid: products destinationId: eu # empty = the default destination Get a starting point from the dashboard Build a task in the wizard, then copy its JSON from the Review step or the task's Config tab, or export all tasks from the task list. Remove createdAt, updatedAt and anything masked (••••••), replace credentials with ${VAR}, and add an id.

export ORDERS_DSN='cdc:secret@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop' meilisearch-cdc -tasks /etc/meilisearch-cdc/tasks.yaml # or CDC_TASKS_FILE=/etc/meilisearch-cdc/tasks.yaml meilisearch-cdc On success the service logs applied tasks file with the path and the number of tasks.

Besides the startup file, tasks can be moved between installations as JSON: GET /api/v1/tasks/export returns every task with secrets masked, and POST /api/v1/tasks/import creates the tasks of a JSON array (stopped). Both are on the task list page as well. See Import and export.
