A connector is a saved source connection: its type and the connection fields of that type. Credentials are stored once, encrypted, and never returned by the API (passwords in connection strings and DynamoDB secret keys come back masked as ••••••). Tasks reference a connector with source.connectorId and add only table-level fields. Connectors with their last test result and the tasks using them. Type Connection fields (connector) Table-level fields (task) postgres dsn schema, table, slot, publication mysql, mariadb dsn, database database, table, serverId mongodb dsn, database database, table (collection) dynamodb region, endpoint, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey table kafka brokers groupId, table (topic) sqlpoll driver, dsn table, cursorColumn, pollInterval couchdb dsn table (database) sqlserver dsn schema, table (and slot, the capture instance, through the API) cockroachdb dsn table (and schema through the API) redis dsn table (stream key) webhook none table (a name for the feed) A task's database overrides the connector's, so one MySQL or MongoDB connector can serve several databases on the same server.

A connector is tested in the background when it is created or saved, and on demand with Test. The result (OK or the error, latency, server version, number of tables) is kept and shown as the last test. The connector page lists what the connector can see: tables and views, collections, topics, streams or databases, with row estimates when the source provides them (at most 1,000 entries, filterable). Creating a task from a listed table pre-fills the wizard. Creating, editing, deleting and testing connectors needs the admin role (the route table does not grant connector tests to moderators).

Saving a connector with the masked password keeps the stored one. Changing a password restarts the running tasks that use the connector. A connector that tasks still use cannot be deleted (409 with the list of tasks).
The API and the tasks file also accept the connection fields directly in a task's source (type, dsn, …) without a connector. The dashboard's wizard always works through a connector.

entries.h: What every source has in common
entries.x: Validation first. Each source checks its prerequisites when the task starts and fails with a message saying what to change. These are permanent errors: the task goes to failed instead of retrying. Position before snapshot. The stream position is captured before the snapshot, so changes made during the copy are replayed afterwards. Lost position → resync. If the stored position no longer exists on the source (purged log, dropped slot, expired shard, trimmed stream), the task logs source position lost and runs a full snapshot again by itself. A primary key. Documents need an id. It comes from the table's primary key, or from mapping.primaryKey when the source has none or you want another one. Value conversion. Times become RFC 3339 strings (or Unix seconds or milliseconds, per task), binary values become base64 strings, NaN and infinities become null, and nested JSON stays nested.

Capture PostgreSQL changes with logical replication (pgoutput): wal_level, REPLICA IDENTITY, replication slots, publications and grants. The PostgreSQL source uses logical replication with the built-in pgoutput plugin: one replication slot and one publication per task, no extensions and no triggers.

Logical replication must be enabled. Set it in postgresql.conf (or with ALTER SYSTEM) and restart the server: ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_level = logical; -- Each running task holds one replication slot and, while streaming, one WAL sender. ALTER SYSTEM SET max_replication_slots = 10; -- at least the number of tasks, plus other consumers ALTER SYSTEM SET max_wal_senders = 10; -- Optional safety net: cap the WAL a forgotten slot can retain (PostgreSQL 13+). ALTER SYSTEM SET max_slot_wal_keep_size = '20GB'; Check with SHOW wal_level;. If it is not logical, the task fails with: postgres: wal_level is "replica" but logical replication needs "logical"; set wal_level = logical in postgresql.conf (or ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_level = logical) and restart the server On managed services the setting has another name: on Amazon RDS and Aurora set the parameter rds.logical_replication = 1 in the parameter group; on Google Cloud SQL set the flag cloudsql.logical_decoding = on; on Azure Database for PostgreSQL set wal_level = logical in the server parameters. Each needs a restart.

The table needs a primary key, or REPLICA IDENTITY FULL, so deletes carry the row's key. Without either the task fails: table public.items has no primary key; add one or run ALTER TABLE "public"."items" REPLICA IDENTITY FULL so deletes can be captured. With REPLICA IDENTITY FULL and no primary key, set mapping.primaryKey to the columns that identify a row. REPLICA IDENTITY NOTHING is refused (deletes would carry no key). Use DEFAULT or FULL. Regular and partitioned tables are supported (relkind r and p); views are not.

The user needs the REPLICATION attribute (to create the slot and stream), SELECT on the table (for the snapshot), and either the right to create the publication or a publication created for it. CREATE ROLE cdc WITH LOGIN REPLICATION PASSWORD 'change-me'; GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE shop TO cdc; GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO cdc; GRANT SELECT ON public.products TO cdc; The publication: by default the task creates one named after itself with CREATE PUBLICATION … FOR TABLE, which PostgreSQL only allows to a user with CREATE on the database who owns the table. If the replication user does not own the table, create the publication yourself as the owner (or a superuser) and enter its name in the task's Publication field: -- as the table owner CREATE PUBLICATION cdc_products FOR TABLE public.products; A publication you name is never altered or dropped by the service; if it does not include the table, the task fails with the ALTER PUBLICATION … ADD TABLE … statement to run. On Amazon RDS, the replication attribute is granted with GRANT rds_replication TO cdc; instead of REPLICATION.

Any connection string the pgx driver accepts, as a URL or in key/value form: postgres://cdc:change-me@db.internal:5432/shop?sslmode=require host=db.internal port=5432 user=cdc password=change-me dbname=shop sslmode=require The database is part of the connection string. The password is masked as •••••• whenever the connector or task is shown.

Field Default Meaning schema public Schema of the table. table required The table whose rows become documents. slot cdc_<task id> Replication slot name. The default is cdc_ plus the task id in lower case with anything outside a-z 0-9 _ replaced by _, cut to 63 bytes. Created when missing. publication same as the slot Publication name. A generated publication is created (or the table added to it) automatically; a named one must already exist.

Snapshot. The table is read in chunks of 5,000 rows (in primary-key order when the table has a primary key). Changes during the copy are replayed afterwards from the slot. Inserts and updates become upserts. Changes are emitted per committed transaction, with the commit time used for lag. Primary key changes (an UPDATE of a key column) delete the old document and write the new one. Deletes delete the document by key. TRUNCATE holds the task unless allowTruncate is on, in which case the index is emptied. Unchanged TOAST values. PostgreSQL does not send large column values (TOASTed text, jsonb, bytea over about 2 kB) that an UPDATE did not change. Those columns are left out of the change. With the default replace write mode the document is replaced without them, so the field disappears from the index until the row is written again. For tables with large values that are updated without changing them, use index.writeMode: upsert, which merges fields into the existing document. Types are decoded from their text form: integers stay integers, numeric and floats become numbers, json and jsonb become nested objects, arrays become arrays, timestamps become times (formatted by mapping.timeFormat) and bytea becomes base64.

Positions are WAL LSNs such as 16/B374D848. Each change carries the end LSN of its transaction's commit, so a checkpoint always covers whole transactions. Once Meilisearch confirms a batch, the slot's confirmed position is advanced (status updates every 10 seconds, well within the default wal_sender_timeout of 60 s), which lets PostgreSQL recycle WAL. While a task is stopped, its slot keeps the WAL it has not confirmed, so nothing is lost, but WAL accumulates on the server. If the slot is invalidated (max_slot_wal_keep_size exceeded) or dropped, the task reports the position as lost and runs a full resync.

When you delete a task with Drop source replication objects checked (the default in the dashboard, dropSource=true in the API), the service terminates the WAL sender still holding the slot, drops the slot, and drops the publication if it generated it. Without it, the slot stays and keeps retaining WAL. Forgotten slots fill disks An unused logical replication slot prevents WAL cleanup forever. Find inactive slots with the query below and drop the ones no task uses. SELECT slot_name, active, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn)) AS behind FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE slot_name LIKE 'cdc_%'; SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('cdc_old_task');

Error Fix create replication slot "cdc_…" (the user needs the REPLICATION attribute and a free max_replication_slots entry) Grant REPLICATION, or raise max_replication_slots (restart), or drop unused slots. replication slot "cdc_…" is active for PID … Another process (often a second installation or an old task with the same id) streams from the slot. Stop it, or give the task its own slot. create publication "cdc_…" (the user needs CREATE on the database and ownership of the table) Create the publication as the table owner and set the task's publication. replication connect (the user needs the REPLICATION attribute) Grant REPLICATION (or rds_replication) and check that pg_hba.conf allows the user to connect. replication slot "cdc_…" was invalidated because its WAL was removed (max_slot_wal_keep_size) Handled automatically with a full resync. Keep tasks running, or raise the limit. table public.x does not exist (or is not visible to this user) Check the schema and table name, and USAGE on the schema.

Capture MySQL 8 and MariaDB changes from the binary log: binlog_format=ROW, binlog_row_image=FULL, server ids, grants and positions. The mysql and mariadb sources read the binary log the way a replica does. Use mysql for MySQL 8 and mariadb for MariaDB; the configuration is the same.

Binary logging must be on, in row format, with full row images. In my.cnf: [mysqld] server-id = 1 # any id, unique in your replication topology log-bin = mysql-bin binlog_format = ROW binlog_row_image = FULL # Keep binlogs long enough to cover a stopped task (7 days here). binlog_expire_logs_seconds = 604800 MySQL 8 enables binary logging and row format by default; check the values with: SELECT @@GLOBAL.log_bin, @@GLOBAL.binlog_format, @@GLOBAL.binlog_row_image; -- MySQL only: must not contain PARTIAL_JSON SELECT @@GLOBAL.binlog_row_value_options; The task fails with a precise message when a setting is wrong, for example: mysql: binlog_format is MIXED but change capture needs ROW; run SET GLOBAL binlog_format = 'ROW' and persist it in the server config mysql: binlog_row_image is MINIMAL but change capture needs FULL; run SET GLOBAL binlog_row_image = 'FULL' and persist it in the server config mysql: binlog_row_value_options = PARTIAL_JSON logs JSON diffs; set it to '' so full values are logged mysql: binary logging is disabled; start the server with --log-bin (and --server-id) On Amazon RDS for MySQL or MariaDB, automated backups enable the binary log; set binlog_format = ROW in the parameter group and extend retention with CALL mysql.rds_set_configuration('binlog retention hours', 168);.

CREATE USER 'cdc'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'change-me'; GRANT REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.* TO 'cdc'@'%'; GRANT SELECT ON shop.products TO 'cdc'@'%'; REPLICATION SLAVE lets the task stream the binlog; REPLICATION CLIENT lets it read the current binlog position and list binlog files; SELECT serves the snapshot and the schema. Missing grants fail the task with the grant to add, for example (grant REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.*).

The go-sql-driver/mysql DSN format. The address must be TCP (the binlog protocol does not use Unix sockets); without a port, 3306 is used. cdc:change-me@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop cdc:change-me@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop?tls=true The database comes from the task's database field, the connector's database field, or the DSN path, in that order. Without any: no database: set source.database or put it in the dsn. The service connects with UTC as the session time zone, so TIMESTAMP values match the binlog.

Field Default Meaning database connector or DSN The database (schema) of the table. table required The table whose rows become documents. serverId derived from the task id The replica server id the task uses when reading the binlog. It must differ from the server's own server-id and from every other replica and task. The default is a stable hash of the task id between 1000 and 231, so two tasks on one server do not disconnect each other.

Snapshot. Keyset pagination over the primary key, 5,000 rows per query. Tables without a primary key are read with a plain scan; they also need mapping.primaryKey so documents have an id. Inserts and updates become upserts, committed per transaction (at the XID event). An update that changes the primary key deletes the old document first. Deletes delete the document. TRUNCATE TABLE on the task's table holds the task unless allowTruncate is on. Other DDL on the table (ALTER, RENAME, …) makes the source reload the column list before decoding further rows. MariaDB JSON columns (stored as LONGTEXT with a json_valid check) are recognised and decoded as JSON.

Positions are binlog coordinates file:offset, for example mysql-bin.000003:1234, taken right after each transaction's commit. The server keeps no per-replica state, so nothing needs cleaning up when a task is deleted. On resume the source checks that the binlog file still exists (SHOW BINARY LOGS); if it was purged, or the server answers with error 1236, the position is lost and the task resyncs automatically. Keep binlog retention longer than any planned downtime. GTIDs are not used: after a failover to another server the coordinates differ, and the task needs a resync (it detects a missing binlog file by itself; otherwise use Resync).

Error Fix read binlog position (the user needs REPLICATION CLIENT) Grant REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.*. binlog replication needs a tcp address Use @tcp(host:port) in the DSN, not @unix(…). binlog mysql-bin.000042 was purged from the server Handled automatically with a full resync. Raise binlog retention. A replica or another task disconnects when the task starts Two binlog readers use the same server id. Set a unique serverId. table shop.x does not exist (or the user cannot see it) Check the database and table, and the SELECT grant.

Capture MongoDB changes with change streams on a replica set or sharded cluster: connection string, _id handling, resume tokens and drops. The MongoDB source watches one collection with a change stream and copies it with a collection scan. Each document's _id becomes the Meilisearch id.

Change streams need a replica set or a sharded cluster. A single-node replica set is enough: mongod --replSet rs0 --bind_ip_all mongosh --eval 'rs.initiate()' On a standalone server the task fails with: mongodb: change streams need a replica set or sharded cluster; start mongod with --replSet and run rs.initiate() (a single node replica set is fine). MongoDB Atlas clusters are replica sets already.

Reading a collection and opening a change stream on it needs the find and changeStream actions on that collection; the built-in read role on the database grants both: use admin db.createUser({ user: "cdc", pwd: "change-me", roles: [{ role: "read", db: "shop" }] })

mongodb://cdc:change-me@mongo1:27017,mongo2:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&authSource=admin mongodb+srv://cdc:change-me@cluster0.example.mongodb.net/ The database is required: set it on the connector (the default database) or in the task, which overrides it. It can also be given in the connection string's path.
Field Meaning database The database; overrides the connector's. table The collection to watch.

Schema. MongoDB has no fixed schema, so the field list shown in the wizard and the schema check is inferred from a $sample of 100 documents. The primary key is always _id. Ids. An ObjectId becomes its 24-character hex string. Other _id types are converted to a string that fits Meilisearch's id alphabet (see document ids). By default the id is written to the field id and _id is not copied; enable Keep key columns to keep it, or set the primary key field to another name. Values. Dates become times (formatted by mapping.timeFormat), Decimal128 becomes a number, embedded documents and arrays stay nested. Inserts, updates and replaces are written with the full current document (the change stream uses fullDocument: updateLookup). A document deleted before the lookup is skipped; its delete follows. Deletes delete by _id. Collection drop, rename or database drop are treated as a truncate: the task is held unless allowTruncate is on. An invalidate event (after a drop or rename) also stops the stream with change stream on … invalidated (collection dropped or renamed); recreate the task to resync.

Positions are change stream resume tokens in extended JSON, for example {"_data":"8263F1…"}. The task resumes right after the stored token. If the token has fallen off the oplog (ChangeStreamHistoryLost, error 286) or is invalid, the position is lost and the task resyncs automatically. Size the oplog to cover the longest time a task may be stopped.

Error Fix source.database is required (or put the database in the dsn path) Set the database on the connector or the task. change streams need a replica set Run mongod with --replSet and rs.initiate(). Connection times out with a single-node replica set in Docker The replica set advertises its member host name; it must resolve from the service. Use ?directConnection=true or a host name both can reach.

Capture Amazon DynamoDB changes through DynamoDB Streams with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES: credentials, IAM permissions, shards and 24h retention. The DynamoDB source copies a table with a parallel scan and then follows its DynamoDB Stream, shard by shard, parents before children.

The table needs a stream whose view type includes new images: NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES (recommended) or NEW_IMAGE. aws dynamodb update-table --table-name products \ --stream-specification StreamEnabled=true,StreamViewType=NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES Without a stream, or with KEYS_ONLY / OLD_IMAGE, the task fails and prints the command above. Changing the view type means disabling the stream and enabling it again, which creates a new stream: resync the task afterwards.

A policy for a dedicated IAM user or role, scoped to the table and its streams: { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:DescribeTable", "dynamodb:Scan"], "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-west-1:123456789012:table/products" }, { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:DescribeStream", "dynamodb:GetShardIterator", "dynamodb:GetRecords"], "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-west-1:123456789012:table/products/stream/*" }, { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:ListTables"], "Resource": "*" } ] } dynamodb:ListTables is only used by the connector's table browser and test.

Field Meaning region Required, for example eu-west-1. endpoint Optional custom endpoint, for example http://localhost:8000 for DynamoDB Local. accessKeyId, secretAccessKey Static credentials. Leave them empty to use the default AWS credential chain of the service's environment (environment variables, shared config and credentials files, EC2/ECS/EKS roles). The secret key is encrypted at rest and masked in the API. The task only adds table, the DynamoDB table name.

Primary key. The table's partition key, followed by its sort key when it has one. A table with both gets a composite document id. Schema. Attributes are inferred from a scan of 100 items; attributes with several types show as mixed. Snapshot. A parallel scan with 4 segments. Inserts and modifications are written from the new image. Removals (including TTL expirations) delete the document by its keys. Values. Numbers without a fraction become integers, sets and lists become arrays, maps become objects, binary becomes base64. DynamoDB has no truncate; deleting the table ends its stream.

A position is a JSON checkpoint holding, for every shard being read, the sequence number of the last record delivered, plus the shards already read to their end and the time the position was first taken. Shards are polled every second and the shard list is refreshed every 10 seconds. Stream records are kept for 24 hours. If a task stays stopped longer, or a shard expires before it was fully read (TrimmedDataAccessException), the position is lost and the task resyncs automatically.

Error Fix dynamodb: table "products" has no stream; enable one with … Run the printed aws dynamodb update-table command. the stream of table "products" has view type KEYS_ONLY; it must include new images Disable the stream, enable it with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES, then resync. source.region is required (or set AWS_REGION) Set the region on the connector. table "products" does not exist in eu-west-1 Check the region and the table name.

Follow the CouchDB or Cloudant _changes feed into Meilisearch: connection URL, database permissions, deletes, design documents and sequences. The CouchDB source copies a database with _all_docs and follows its _changes feed. It works with Apache CouchDB, IBM Cloudant and other servers that speak the CouchDB replication protocol.

Nothing to enable on the server: the _changes feed is always available. The user needs read access to the database: an admin, or a member (reader) listed in the database's _security object: curl -X PUT http://admin:secret@couch.internal:5984/_users/org.couchdb.user:cdc \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name":"cdc","password":"change-me","roles":[],"type":"user"}' curl -X PUT http://admin:secret@couch.internal:5984/products/_security \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"admins":{"names":[],"roles":[]},"members":{"names":["cdc"],"roles":[]}}' Note that setting _security replaces the whole object; merge it with existing members.
The server URL with optional basic-auth credentials. The database name goes in the task, not in the URL: http://cdc:change-me@couch.internal:5984 https://cdc:change-me@account.cloudant.com
Field Meaning table The CouchDB database to follow (the source uses database when table is empty).

Primary key. The document _id. CouchDB ids may contain characters Meilisearch does not allow in ids; they are escaped (see document ids). Schema. Inferred from a sample of 100 documents. Design documents (_design/…) are skipped everywhere. Attachment stubs (_attachments) are removed from documents; _rev is kept. Snapshot. _all_docs with include_docs=true, 1,000 documents per page. Changes are read with feed=longpoll (requests wait up to 30 seconds for changes), 1,000 changes per request. A change with "deleted": true deletes the document; other changes upsert the winning revision. Transient HTTP failures are retried inside the source up to 5 times in a row before the task's own retry takes over. CouchDB has no truncate. Deleting the database stops the task with a permanent error.

Positions are the feed's opaque update sequences, kept verbatim (12-g1AAAA… on CouchDB 2 and later, 12 on 1.x). Resuming from one continues with the following changes; CouchDB may replay a few, which is harmless. If the server rejects a stored sequence, the position is lost and the task resyncs.

Error Fix couchdb: authentication failed …; check the user and password in the dsn Fix the credentials in the URL. couchdb: the user may not read database "products" …; add it to the database _security members Add the user to the database's _security members. couchdb: database "products" not found … Create the database or fix the task's table. couchdb: invalid dsn …: want http(s)://user:password@host:5984 Use an absolute http or https URL.

Capture SQL Server changes from native CDC change tables: sp_cdc_enable_db, sp_cdc_enable_table, SQL Server Agent, grants and retention. The SQL Server source reads the change tables of SQL Server's built-in change data capture (CDC). CDC must be enabled on the database and the table, and SQL Server Agent must run.

As a member of sysadmin (for the database) and db_owner (for the table): USE shop; EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db; EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_table @source_schema = N'dbo', @source_name = N'products', @role_name = NULL; This creates the capture instance dbo_products, its change table cdc.dbo_products_CT, and the capture and cleanup jobs. With @role_name = NULL no gating role is required to read the changes; if you set a role, add the CDC user to it.

The Agent runs the capture job that fills the change tables. When the source can see that the Agent is stopped, the task fails with: sqlserver: SQL Server Agent is stopped, so the CDC capture job does not run; start it (Linux containers: MSSQL_AGENT_ENABLED=true) In the official Linux container, set MSSQL_AGENT_ENABLED=true. The check reads sys.dm_server_services; it is skipped where that view does not exist (Azure SQL Database) or when the user lacks VIEW SERVER STATE.

USE shop; CREATE LOGIN cdc WITH PASSWORD = 'Change-me-123'; CREATE USER cdc FOR LOGIN cdc; GRANT SELECT ON dbo.products TO cdc; -- snapshot GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA::cdc TO cdc; -- change tables and cdc.lsn_time_mapping -- optional, lets the task detect a stopped Agent: USE master; GRANT VIEW SERVER STATE TO cdc;

sqlserver://cdc:Change-me-123@sql.internal:1433?database=shop sqlserver://cdc:Change-me-123@sql.internal:1433?database=shop&encrypt=true&trustservercertificate=false The database must be in the connection string (?database=) or in the task's database. Connected to master, tempdb, model or msdb, the task fails and asks for the database.

Field Default Meaning schema dbo Schema of the table. table required The CDC-enabled table. slot (API only) {schema}_{table} The capture instance to read. When the default does not exist, the newest capture instance of the table is used. Useful during a schema change, when a table has two capture instances.

Primary key required. The table needs a primary key, and the capture instance must capture every key column. Captured columns only. Only the columns captured by the capture instance are read. A column added to the table after the capture instance was created is not captured; create a new capture instance (and pass it as slot) to include it. Snapshot. Keyset pages of 5,000 rows. Changes are polled every 500 ms, up to 5,000 change rows at a time. This adds to the capture job's own latency, a few seconds by default. Inserts and updates upsert; deletes delete. Commit times come from cdc.lsn_time_mapping, which SQL Server records in server local time; they are reported as UTC, so lag is off by the server's UTC offset when the server does not run in UTC.

Positions are lsnhex:seqvalhex: the __$start_lsn and __$seqval of the last change row delivered, 20 lowercase hex digits each, for example 0000002b000004880021:0000002b000004880020. The task resumes strictly after it. The cleanup job removes change rows older than its retention period (3 days by default). A position older than the capture instance's minimum LSN is lost and the task resyncs automatically. A task that is idle (no changes) for longer than the retention also sees this, because its stored position stops moving while the low-water mark advances.

Error Fix change data capture is not enabled for database "shop"; as sysadmin run: USE [shop]; EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db; Run the printed statement. table dbo.products is not tracked by change data capture; run: EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_table … Run the printed statement. read cdc.change_tables (the user needs SELECT on the cdc schema) GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA::cdc TO cdc; capture instance "dbo_products" no longer exists (CDC was disabled for the table?) Enable CDC on the table again, then resync. SQL Server Agent is stopped … Start the Agent.

Capture CockroachDB changes with a core changefeed: kv.rangefeed.enabled, CHANGEFEED privilege, HLC positions and gc.ttlseconds. The CockroachDB source uses a core (sinkless) changefeed, which needs no enterprise license and no Kafka or cloud-storage sink. The snapshot is a consistent read at the changefeed's starting timestamp.

Changefeeds need rangefeeds. If kv.rangefeed.enabled is false, the task tries to enable it; when the user may not change cluster settings, the task fails and asks an admin to run: SET CLUSTER SETTING kv.rangefeed.enabled = true; The table needs an explicit primary key. A table that only has CockroachDB's hidden rowid is refused with a hint to run ALTER TABLE … ALTER PRIMARY KEY USING COLUMNS (…).

CREATE USER cdc WITH PASSWORD 'change-me'; GRANT SELECT, CHANGEFEED ON TABLE shop.public.products TO cdc; Missing privileges fail the task with (the user needs SELECT and CHANGEFEED privileges on the table).

CockroachDB speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol; use a PostgreSQL URL with the database in the path: postgresql://cdc:change-me@crdb.internal:26257/shop?sslmode=verify-full postgresql://root@localhost:26257/shop?sslmode=disable # insecure local cluster
Field Default Meaning table required The table in the connection's database. schema (API only) public Schema of the table.

Snapshot. Keyset pages of 5,000 rows read AS OF SYSTEM TIME the position captured before the copy, so the copy is consistent and the changefeed continues exactly from there. Stream. CREATE CHANGEFEED FOR TABLE … WITH updated, resolved = '1s', format = json, cursor = '…' (older versions fall back to EXPERIMENTAL CHANGEFEED FOR). Rows are read as JSON in both phases, so they carry identical values: numbers become integers or floats, TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ become times, other values stay as CockroachDB renders them in JSON. Deletes arrive as rows with a null after image and delete the document. Truncates are not captured by changefeeds; resync the task after a TRUNCATE.

Positions are CockroachDB HLC timestamps in decimal form, for example 1700000000123456789.0000000001. Changefeed rows are only ordered per key, so every event carries the latest resolved timestamp seen so far: everything at or before it has been delivered, and restarting from it replays at most a few changes. A position older than the table's garbage collection window (gc.ttlseconds) cannot be resumed; the task resyncs automatically. Keep tasks running, or raise the TTL for tables whose tasks may be stopped for long.

Error Fix changefeeds need rangefeeds, but kv.rangefeed.enabled is false and this user cannot change it Run SET CLUSTER SETTING kv.rangefeed.enabled = true as an admin. table public.x has no primary key (it uses the hidden rowid column) Add a primary key. table public.x does not exist in the current database Put the right database in the connection string.

Consume Debezium change events from Kafka with the JSON converter to sync Oracle, Db2, Cassandra and other databases into Meilisearch. The Kafka source consumes Debezium change events from a topic. Anything Debezium captures (Oracle, Db2, Cassandra, Informix, Vitess, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL…) can feed Meilisearch this way.

A Debezium connector writing one table's changes to one topic, typically <topic.prefix>.<schema>.<table>. The JSON converter for keys and values, with or without schemas. Avro and Protobuf are not supported. Brokers reachable from the service in plaintext: the connector takes a list of host:port brokers and has no SASL or TLS settings. { "name": "inventory-connector", "config": { "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector", "topic.prefix": "dbserver1", "table.include.list": "inventory.customers", "key.converter": "org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter", "value.converter": "org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter", "key.converter.schemas.enable": "true", "value.converter.schemas.enable": "true" } } (Database connection settings of the Debezium connector are omitted; see the Debezium documentation for your database.)
Field Meaning brokers One or more host:port seed brokers, for example kafka-1:9092, kafka-2:9092.

Field Default Meaning table required The Debezium topic, for example dbserver1.inventory.customers. A missing topic fails with a hint to check topic.prefix and the table include list. groupId cdc-<task id> The consumer group whose committed offsets track progress. Never share it with other consumers.

Envelope. Messages may be wrapped as {"schema": …, "payload": …} or be the bare envelope. Debezium's op is mapped: c, u and r (snapshot read) upsert the after image; d deletes using the before image, or the message key when there is none; t is a truncate. Tombstones (empty values after a delete), heartbeats, schema changes and transaction metadata are skipped. Types. With schemas enabled, Debezium logical types are converted: io.debezium.time.Timestamp, MicroTimestamp, NanoTimestamp, ZonedTimestamp, Date and Kafka Connect Timestamp/Date become times; org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Decimal becomes a number. Schema and key. Columns are inferred from up to 50 messages read in at most 5 seconds from the start of the topic. The primary key comes from the message key's fields (id when it cannot be determined); set mapping.primaryKey to override it. Snapshot. Replays the topic from its start up to the current end offsets and keeps the latest image per message key in memory, then writes the rows still alive. Memory grows with the number of live rows. Very large topics Use the stream sync mode instead of snapshot_stream: the topic is consumed from the group's committed offsets, or from the earliest offset when the group has none, as ordinary change events, without holding the table in memory. Debezium's own snapshot (op: r) then fills the index.

A position is a JSON object mapping topic/partition to the next offset to read. Confirmed positions are also committed to the consumer group, so tools like kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group cdc-<task> show the task's lag. If an offset is no longer available (topic retention removed it), the position is lost and the task resyncs automatically.

Error Fix kafka: topic "…" does not exist; check the Debezium connector topic.prefix and table include list Use the exact topic name Debezium writes. kafka: delete without before image or key Keep the message key (do not drop it in an SMT), or enable before images on the source. Decoding errors on every message The topic uses Avro or Protobuf; switch the connector to the JSON converter.

Push changes into a Redis stream with XADD and sync them into Meilisearch: entry format, op field, positions and trimming. The Redis source reads a Redis stream that your application appends changes to with XADD. Use it when your code already knows what changed and Redis sits next to it.

Append one entry per change. Fields: Field Meaning op upsert (default; insert, update and replace are aliases), delete or truncate. Any other value stops the task with entry … has unknown op. id The document key. It is copied into the row as id unless the row already has an id. data Optional JSON object with the whole row. Without data, every other field except op becomes a column, as a string (Redis field values are strings). XADD items * op upsert id 42 data '{"name":"shoe","price":9.5,"tags":["sale"]}' XADD items * id 42 name shoe price 9.5 # same row, values as strings XADD items * op delete id 42 XADD items * op truncate # holds the task unless allowTruncate Prefer data with JSON when you need numbers, booleans or nested values in Meilisearch (for filters and sorting).

redis://:password@redis.internal:6379/0 redis://cdc:password@redis.internal:6379/0 # Redis 6+ ACL user rediss://cdc:password@redis.internal:6380/0 # TLS The user needs to read the stream: with ACLs, for example ACL SETUSER cdc on >password ~items +ping +type +xrange +xrevrange +xread +xinfo|stream +scan (SCAN is only used by the connector's stream browser). The key must be a stream or not exist yet; any other type fails with key "items" is a hash, not a stream.
Field Meaning table The stream key, for example items. The primary key is always id. The schema shown in the wizard is inferred from a sample of entries.

Snapshot. A stream is a log, not a table: the snapshot replays the whole stream from the beginning, keeps the latest image per key (like a compacted log) and writes the rows still alive at the end. That image is held in memory. Stream. XREAD without a consumer group, 1,000 entries at a time, blocking at most 500 ms per call. The task's groupId is ignored, nothing is acknowledged in Redis, and the service never trims the stream. Trim it yourself (XADD … MAXLEN ~ … or XTRIM) with a margin that covers task downtime.

Positions are stream entry ids such as 1700000000000-0; 0-0 is the start. On resume the source checks that nothing after the position was trimmed or deleted, and that the stream was not recreated (a position after the last generated id). Otherwise the position is lost and the task resyncs. The precise checks use fields of XINFO STREAM added in Redis 7.

Poll any PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite table with an incrementing cursor column when log-based capture is not available; soft deletes and limits. When log-based capture is not available (no replication privileges, a managed database that hides its log, SQLite), the sqlpoll source re-reads a table on an interval and picks up rows whose cursor column moved forward.

A driver: pgx (PostgreSQL; postgres and postgresql are aliases), mysql (MySQL and MariaDB; alias mariadb) or sqlite (alias sqlite3). A primary key, used to page through rows: table … has no primary key; sqlpoll needs one to page through rows otherwise. A cursor column that grows with every insert and update: an updated_at timestamp maintained by the application or a trigger, or a version number bumped on every write. SELECT on the table. No other privilege is needed. Example for PostgreSQL, keeping updated_at current with a trigger: ALTER TABLE products ADD COLUMN updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(); CREATE INDEX ON products (updated_at, id); CREATE FUNCTION touch_updated_at() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN NEW.updated_at := clock_timestamp(); RETURN NEW; END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql; CREATE TRIGGER products_touch BEFORE UPDATE ON products FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION touch_updated_at(); For MySQL: updated_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6). An index on the cursor column (followed by the key) keeps each poll cheap.
Driver DSN example pgx postgres://reader:secret@db.internal:5432/shop mysql reader:secret@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop (parseTime is enabled automatically) sqlite file:/var/data/app.sqlite

Field Default Meaning table required The table to poll. schema (API only) driver default Schema of the table. cursorColumn required The column that grows with every write. The wizard ranks candidates (updated_at, modified_at, last_modified, changed_at, version, row_version, rowversion, then timestamps and integers). pollInterval 2s How often to look for changes. The wizard offers 500 ms to 1 minute; any duration works through the API.

Snapshot. Keyset pages of 1,000 rows by primary key. Polling. Every interval, the source reads rows whose (cursor, primary key) is greater than the last one delivered, 1,000 at a time, and keeps reading until a page comes back short. Each row becomes an upsert. Deletes need soft deletes. A hard DELETE is invisible: the row simply stops being returned. Mark rows deleted instead (a deleted flag or a deleted_at column that also bumps the cursor) and set the task's soft delete column, so those rows delete their documents.

Rows whose cursor is NULL are never streamed (the snapshot still copies them). A write that commits with a cursor lower than one already polled is missed: for example a long transaction that stamped updated_at at its start, or sequence values allocated out of order. Prefer a cursor assigned at commit time, or keep transactions short compared with the poll interval. A periodic diff and repair catches anything missed. On SQLite prefer an integer cursor: time values are bound as text and compare lexically against however the column was written. No truncate detection.

A position is JSON with the cursor and primary key of the last row delivered, for example {"cursor":"2026-10-26T10:00:00.123456Z","pk":[42]}. A null cursor means "from the beginning" (the table was empty when the position was taken). A position that cannot be decoded is treated as lost and the task resyncs.

Push changes to meilisearch-cdc over HTTP: the /api/v1/ingest endpoint, JSON, array and NDJSON payloads, responses and retries. A webhook task has no database to read: your application POSTs its changes to /api/v1/ingest/{task id}, and the request returns once the documents are confirmed in Meilisearch.

Create a connector of type Webhook. It has no connection settings. Create a task on it. The table is only a name for the feed (it appears in logs). Set a primary key column in the mapping step if your rows do not have an id field. Optionally add a signing secret (see signed requests). Generate creates a random whsec_… value; copy it then, because it is never shown again. Start the task. Its Overview tab shows a Push endpoint card with the URL and, for signed tasks, a ready-to-run signed curl example. The task id is in the URL, so give the task a readable id (for example products-push) when you create it.

The body is a single change, a JSON array of changes, or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), up to 64 MiB: {"op": "upsert", "row": {"id": 1, "name": "Desk lamp", "price": 39.9}} [ {"op": "upsert", "row": {"id": 1, "name": "Desk lamp"}}, {"op": "delete", "row": {"id": 2}}, {"row": {"id": 3, "name": "Chair"}} ] {"op":"upsert","row":{"id":4,"name":"Shelf"}} {"op":"delete","row":{"id":5}} Field Meaning op upsert (default; insert, update and replace are aliases), delete or truncate. row The row as a JSON object. Required and non-empty for upserts and deletes; a delete needs at least the key columns. Integral numbers become integers, others floats. Changes in one request are applied in order, and requests to one task are applied in the order they arrive. A truncate holds the task unless allowTruncate is on.

Status Meaning 200 {"accepted":n,"position":"…"} Every change is durably in Meilisearch. 400 Invalid payload (the error says why), or the task is not a webhook task. 401 Not authenticated, or the signature is missing, wrong, or stale. 403 Authenticated, but the role is below moderator. 503 the task is not running; start it and retry. 504 changes were not confirmed in time; retry (writes are idempotent) after 60 seconds. Retry on 503, 504 and network errors: the same change applied twice gives the same document.

How a push authenticates depends on whether the task has a signing secret (source.webhookSecret): Task What the request needs No secret A bearer token or session with at least the moderator role. The static CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN works: Authorization: Bearer …. Secret set A valid signature. No token is needed, and a token alone is refused with 401. Anonymous callers get 401 both for unknown task ids and for tasks without a secret, so task ids cannot be probed. # Task without a secret: a token with the moderator role or higher curl -X POST "https://cdc.example.com/api/v1/ingest/products-push" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"op":"upsert","row":{"id":1,"name":"Desk lamp"}}'

With a signing secret (at least 16 characters), each request carries two headers: X-CDC-Timestamp: 1767225600 X-CDC-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + raw body)> The timestamp is in Unix seconds and must be within 5 minutes of the server clock. The HMAC covers the timestamp, a dot, and the exact bytes of the body, so sign what you send. A request is refused with 401 when it is unsigned (the request is not signed: send the X-CDC-Timestamp and X-CDC-Signature headers), signed with another secret or over a changed body (the signature does not match …), or too old or too far in the future (the signature timestamp is outside the accepted 5 minute window; check the sender's clock).

CDC=https://cdc.example.com TASK=products-push SECRET='whsec_…' # the task's signing secret BODY='{"op":"upsert","row":{"id":1,"name":"Desk lamp"}}' TS=$(date +%s) SIG=$(printf '%s.%s' "$TS" "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SECRET" | sed 's/^.* //') curl -X POST "$CDC/api/v1/ingest/$TASK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H "X-CDC-Timestamp: $TS" -H "X-CDC-Signature: sha256=$SIG" -d "$BODY"

import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'; async function push(changes) { const body = JSON.stringify(changes); const ts = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000).toString(); const sig = createHmac('sha256', process.env.CDC_WEBHOOK_SECRET).update(`${ts}.${body}`).digest('hex'); const res = await fetch('https://cdc.example.com/api/v1/ingest/products-push', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-CDC-Timestamp': ts, 'X-CDC-Signature': `sha256=${sig}` }, body, }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status} ${await res.text()}`); return res.json(); // {accepted, position} }

The secret is encrypted at rest and returned masked (••••••). In the task's Edit page, Rotate generates a new one and Remove clears it (the API takes "" to remove it; sending the mask back keeps the stored one). The X-CDC-Signature header may hold several comma-separated signatures, and any one that matches is accepted, so a sender can sign with both the old and the new secret while you switch.

Positions are a per-task sequence number (0, 1, 2…), one per pushed change. Pushes are queued in memory (64 requests wait at most; further pushers block) and are not kept across restarts: a push that was not confirmed when the service stopped fails, and the sender must retry. The schema is a single id column (the primary key unless the mapping names another). Do not resync a webhook task The webhook source has nothing to copy: its snapshot is empty. A Resync (or a Reset checkpoint while zero-downtime resync is on) rebuilds the index from nothing: an in-place resync clears it, and a zero-downtime rebuild swaps in an empty shadow index. Your application then has to push every document again. Use the stream sync mode for webhook tasks: it refuses resyncs (409, resync needs a snapshot). Never use snapshot mode.

Add Meilisearch instances as destinations: URL, API key permissions, gzip, timeout, health checks, the default destination and per-instance pages. A destination is a named Meilisearch instance that tasks write to. Add as many as you need (regions, staging, a search replica) and fan one table out to several of them with several tasks. Destinations with live health, version, documents and the tasks writing to each.

Go to Destinations → Add destination (admin role). Test checks the URL and key before saving and reports the version, latency and number of indexes. Field Default Meaning Name required A label shown everywhere, for example Production (EU). URL required Absolute http or https URL of the instance, for example https://ms-1234.meilisearch.io. A trailing slash is removed. API key empty The key sent as a bearer token. Stored encrypted, shown as ••••••; keep the mask to keep the stored key. Gzip requests on in the dashboard Compress request bodies. Saves bandwidth to remote instances; turn it off on loopback or a LAN to save CPU. In the API the JSON field gzip is false when omitted. Timeout 30s Per-request timeout. Health check every 30s Background check interval, between 5s and 1h. The dashboard offers 5 s to 10 minutes; the API accepts any value in range. Tags, description empty For your own organisation. The first destination becomes the default: tasks that do not name a destination write there, and index pages open on it. Make default moves the flag. A task's empty index.destinationId is resolved to the default when the task is saved, so later changing the default does not move existing tasks.

The simplest choice is the instance's master key or its Default Admin API Key. If you create a dedicated key, include the actions the features you use need. These follow from the Meilisearch API calls the service makes: Feature Meilisearch actions Syncing (snapshot and stream) documents.add, documents.delete, indexes.create, indexes.get, indexes.update (primary key of an empty index), stats.get, tasks.get Managed index settings settings.get, settings.update Zero-downtime resync indexes.create, indexes.swap, indexes.delete, settings.get, settings.update, tasks.get; plus dumps.create with dump before resync Health checks version, stats.get (the /health route needs no key) Dashboard: search, documents, diff search, documents.get Dashboard: task queue, backups tasks.get, tasks.cancel, dumps.create, snapshots.create Dashboard: index admin indexes.delete, indexes.swap, settings.update, and the compaction action of your Meilisearch version Scope the key's indexes to the index uids your tasks use, plus *__cdc_shadow_* if you enable zero-downtime resync (shadow indexes are named <uid>__cdc_shadow_<unix time>). Experimental features use Meilisearch's /experimental-features route, which may need the master key. A rejected key stops tasks with a configuration error (invalid_api_key), rather than retrying.

Every destination is checked in the background at its interval. A check reads the version, the number of indexes and documents and the database size, and records the latency. The destination page and list show: healthy or unreachable, with the last error and the number of consecutive failures; version, indexes, documents, database size, latency, the last time it was healthy and the next check; the tasks writing to it with their state, index, lag, rate and last sync, and an aggregate (tasks, running, failing, last sync, maximum lag, rate). Each completed check is pushed live to dashboards (destination.health events). Check now runs one immediately (moderator). Testing a destination's connection needs admin. An alert rule of type meili_down notifies you when an instance stays unreachable; see Alerts.

Changing the URL or the API key restarts the running tasks that write to the destination. A new interval takes effect at once. A destination used by tasks cannot be deleted (409 with the tasks), and the default destination cannot be deleted; make another one the default first.

Each destination has its own page with tabs: The detail page of one Meilisearch instance. Tab What it shows Overview Health, statistics and the tasks writing here. Indexes The instance's indexes with document counts and the tasks that manage them. See Index management. Meilisearch tasks The instance's task queue, filterable by index, status and type; enqueued tasks can be cancelled (moderator). Writes made by meilisearch-cdc carry the custom metadata cdc:<task id>. Backups Request a dump or a snapshot of the instance (admin). Meilisearch writes them to its own dump and snapshot directories. Experimental Meilisearch's experimental features as toggles (admin; read only for others). Settings The destination's own fields (name, URL, key, gzip, timeout, interval). The top-level Indexes and Meilisearch tasks pages show the same information for every instance at once, grouped per instance.

When MEILI_URL is set, the service writes only to that instance. It appears as destination default, marked managed by env, with its URL and key read only, and adding, deleting or switching destinations is refused with 409. See Configuration.

Every field of a meilisearch-cdc task, step by step through the wizard: source scope, mapping, primary keys, index, write mode, sync and safety. A task connects one source table to one Meilisearch index. The wizard walks through six steps; every option it shows maps to a field of the task JSON used by the API and the tasks file. Open Tasks → New task (admin role). The steps are Connector, Source, Mapping, Index, Sync & safety and Review. Errors are shown on the step they belong to, and the review lists anything left to fix.

Pick the saved connector to read from, or add one from the side panel without leaving the wizard. Credentials live in the connector only; the task never repeats them. See Connectors. Step 1: choose a connector.

Basics, then what to sync: Field JSON Notes Name name Required. Task id id Optional. Letters, digits, - and _, at most 64 characters. The wizard derives it from the name when empty; the API generates a random one. It cannot change later and names the replication slot, consumer group and webhook URL. Description, tags description, tags Tags filter the task list. Table (or collection, topic, stream…) source.table Required. Pick from the tables the connector lists, or type it. Source-specific fields source.schema, source.database, source.slot, source.publication, source.serverId, source.groupId, source.cursorColumn, source.pollInterval, source.webhookSecret Shown only for the sources that use them; each source page explains them. Test connection (moderator) connects through the connector, reads the table's schema and transforms five sample rows with the current mapping, so you see real documents before anything is written. It uses POST /api/v1/tasks/test. For PostgreSQL, testing also creates the task's publication if it does not exist yet.
The mapping turns rows into documents. Step 3: document identity, fields, transforms and static fields.

Field JSON Default Meaning Primary key columns mapping.primaryKey the source's primary key Source columns that identify a row. Several columns build a composite id. Required when the source has no primary key. Primary key field mapping.primaryKeyField id The document field that holds the id; it becomes the index's primary key. Keep key columns mapping.keepKeyColumns off Also copy the original key columns into the document. Off: a key column is left out, unless it is the single key column and has the same name as the primary key field. How document ids are built A single integer key is written as a number (42). Other single keys are written as strings. Values made only of a-z A-Z 0-9 - (integers, UUIDs, slugs) are kept as they are. Anything else is escaped into Meilisearch's id alphabet: _ becomes __ and every other byte becomes _XX (hex). For example user@example.com becomes user_40example_2Ecom. Escaped ids always contain _ and raw ones never do, so two different keys never collide. Composite keys join their escaped parts with - (a - inside a part is escaped too): (7, "fr") becomes 7-fr. Ids longer than 511 bytes are replaced by h- and a SHA-256 hex digest. A row without a value for a key column cannot become a document; it goes to the dead letter queue as a transform entry and the checkpoint moves on. Two tasks may write to the same index (with the upsert write mode, to merge fields from several tables), but only with the same primary key field: saving a task whose key field differs from another task on that index and destination fails with 409.

Field JSON Meaning Include mapping.include Copy only these columns (key columns are always available for the id). Empty copies every column. Exclude mapping.exclude Drop these columns. Applied after include. Rename mapping.rename Map of source column to document field, for example {"customer_email": "email"}.

Field JSON Meaning Soft delete column and value mapping.softDeleteColumn, mapping.softDeleteValue Rows whose column matches turn into deletes. With an empty value, any non-null value deletes (a deleted_at timestamp, say), except boolean false. With a value, the column's text is compared case-insensitively, for example true or 1. Geo latitude and longitude columns mapping.geo.lat, mapping.geo.lng Build Meilisearch's _geo field {"lat": …, "lng": …} from two numeric (or numeric string) columns. When either is missing or not a number, _geo is written as null. Add _geo to the filterable and sortable attributes to use geosearch. The source columns themselves are still copied unless excluded. Time format mapping.timeFormat rfc3339 (default; ISO 8601 strings in UTC, readable but not usable for range filters or chronological sorting), unix (seconds since the epoch: filterable and sortable numbers) or unix_ms (milliseconds).

mapping.static adds the same fields to every document, for example {"tenant": "acme", "source": "eu-db"}. This is handy for multi-tenant indexes fed by several tasks. Static fields overwrite source columns of the same name; the primary key field always wins.

Step 4: destination, index uid, write mode and managed settings. Field JSON Default Meaning Destination index.destinationId the default destination The Meilisearch instance to write to. Index uid index.uid the table name Required; a-z A-Z 0-9 - _, up to 400 characters. Created on first write when missing, with the primary key field as its primary key. The wizard suggests existing indexes and shows their document count and other writers. Write mode index.writeMode replace replace sends whole documents (Meilisearch POST /documents): fields removed in the source disappear. upsert merges fields into existing documents (PUT /documents): useful when several tasks write one index, or when the source omits unchanged columns (PostgreSQL TOAST). In upsert mode a document deleted and re-created in the same batch is replaced, so stale fields do not come back. Manage index settings index.manageSettings off Apply index.settings when the task starts (and when you save it while stopped), and report drift in the schema check. Settings index.settings none Meilisearch index settings, the same JSON as Meilisearch's PATCH /indexes/{uid}/settings. Only the keys you set are managed. Edited with the settings editor. Unknown keys are rejected.

Mode JSON Behaviour Snapshot + stream snapshot_stream (default) Copy the existing rows, then stream every change. The usual choice. Stream only stream Start from the current position; existing rows are not copied. Resync is refused in this mode. Snapshot only snapshot Copy the rows once; the task then shows completed and stops.

Field JSON Default Meaning Batch size sync.batchSize 1000 Documents per Meilisearch request. Larger batches index faster and use more memory; 5,000 to 10,000 suits big snapshots. Flush interval sync.flushInterval 1s The longest a change waits in a partial batch. Lower it for lower latency on quiet tables. Max in-flight sync.maxInflight 4 Batches sent to Meilisearch and not yet confirmed. Meilisearch auto-batches consecutive tasks, so 8 helps bulk loads. Within a batch, changes to the same document are coalesced and only the final state is sent. Confirmations are processed in order, so checkpoints never skip an unconfirmed batch. See Performance and tuning.

Field JSON Default Meaning Max attempts sync.retry.maxAttempts 8 Attempts for one Meilisearch write before the pipeline gives up and restarts. Initial backoff sync.retry.initialBackoff 200ms First wait; waits grow exponentially with full jitter. Max backoff sync.retry.maxBackoff 30s Upper bound of a wait. Network errors, Meilisearch 5xx, 429 and 408 are retried. A payload that is too large is split in half. Documents Meilisearch rejects are isolated into the dead letter queue. Configuration errors (a bad API key, an index whose primary key differs) stop the task as failed. When the attempts run out, the pipeline restarts with its own backoff (1 s up to 1 minute) and the task shows retrying.

Field JSON Wizard default API default Meaning Max delete ratio sync.safety.maxDeleteRatio 0.2 (20%) 0 (off) Hold the task when one flush would delete more than this share of the index (0 to 1; 0 disables the guard). Min docs for delete guard sync.safety.minDocsForDeleteGuard 1000 1000 The ratio check is skipped while the index has fewer documents. Allow TRUNCATE sync.safety.allowTruncate off off Let a source truncate (or a dropped MongoDB collection) delete every document. When off, the task is held. Zero-downtime resync sync.safety.zeroDowntimeResync on off Rebuild into a shadow index and swap it in when complete, so search keeps working during a resync. Dump before resync sync.safety.dumpBeforeResync off off Ask Meilisearch for a dump before a zero-downtime rebuild starts (best effort: a failed dump is logged, the rebuild continues). A held task has stopped before applying the risky batch, so nothing was lost and nothing was deleted. Look at the source, then Resume (the batch is retried, and holds again if the guard still applies), raise the guard, or Resync. The hold reason is in the task's status, for example safety hold: a single batch would delete 5000 of 8000 documents (62% > 20% limit) or safety hold: the source table was truncated; enable safety.allowTruncate or resync the task. The delete guard reads the index size at most every 10 seconds.

The review summarises the task, shows its JSON and lists any field that needs attention. Create saves it stopped; Create & start starts it right away (API: POST /api/v1/tasks?start=true). Validation errors come back as 422 with one message per problem.

The full shape accepted by POST /api/v1/tasks, PUT /api/v1/tasks/{id}, import and the tasks file. Defaults are applied when a field is empty or zero. { "id": "products", "name": "Postgres products", "description": "Catalog search", "tags": ["shop"], "desiredState": "running", "source": { "connectorId": "pg-main", "type": "postgres", "dsn": "postgres://cdc:secret@db:5432/shop", "database": "", "schema": "public", "table": "products", "slot": "", "publication": "", "serverId": 0, "region": "", "endpoint": "", "accessKeyId": "", "secretAccessKey": "", "brokers": [], "groupId": "", "driver": "", "cursorColumn": "", "pollInterval": "2s", "webhookSecret": "" }, "mapping": { "primaryKey": ["id"], "primaryKeyField": "id", "keepKeyColumns": false, "include": [], "exclude": ["internal_notes"], "rename": {"customer_email": "email"}, "softDeleteColumn": "deleted_at", "softDeleteValue": "", "geo": {"lat": "lat", "lng": "lng"}, "timeFormat": "unix", "static": {"tenant": "acme"} }, "index": { "uid": "products", "destinationId": "", "writeMode": "replace", "manageSettings": true, "settings": {"filterableAttributes": ["category"], "sortableAttributes": ["price"]} }, "sync": { "mode": "snapshot_stream", "batchSize": 1000, "flushInterval": "1s", "maxInflight": 4, "retry": {"maxAttempts": 8, "initialBackoff": "200ms", "maxBackoff": "30s"}, "safety": { "maxDeleteRatio": 0.2, "minDocsForDeleteGuard": 1000, "allowTruncate": false, "zeroDowntimeResync": true, "dumpBeforeResync": false } } } Use connectorId or the inline connection fields (type, dsn, …), not both: with a connector, the connector's connection fields are used and type is taken from it. Durations are strings ("500ms", "2s"); a plain number is read as milliseconds. desiredState is running, stopped or paused; the API sets it through actions, the tasks file through this field. Responses add createdAt, updatedAt and a status object, and mask secrets as ••••••. Sending a masked value back keeps the stored secret.

Task states and lifecycle actions (start, pause, resync, reset checkpoint), editing, batch actions, import and export, and the task detail tabs. Every task has a live state, a set of lifecycle actions and a detail page with its counters, logs and data-quality tools. The task list: search, filter by source, state or tag, and select several tasks for batch actions.

State Meaning stopped Not running. The checkpoint is kept. starting Connecting to the source, preparing the index and applying managed settings. snapshotting Copying existing rows, with progress (done / total; the total is an estimate from the source). resyncing A snapshot requested by Resync or by a lost source position. streaming Applying changes in near real time. retrying The pipeline failed with a transient error and restarts after a backoff (1 s, doubling up to 1 minute; the status shows the attempt and the wait). The backoff starts over after two minutes of healthy running. paused Stopped by Pause. Like stopped, but kept paused across service restarts. held A safety guard stopped the task before a mass delete or a truncate. It needs an operator. failed A configuration error retrying cannot fix (bad credentials, missing table, wrong server settings, primary key mismatch). Fix it, then start again. completed A snapshot-mode task finished its copy. When the service starts, tasks whose desired state is running start again from their checkpoints; paused tasks stay paused.

Action Role What it does Start / Resume moderator Runs the task from its checkpoint (a snapshot first if it never finished one). Stop moderator Drains pending batches (up to CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT) and stops. Unconfirmed changes are replayed on the next start. Pause moderator Like stop, but the state is paused. Restart moderator Stop, then start. Resync moderator Rebuilds the index from a fresh snapshot, then streams from the position captured before it. With zero-downtime resync the copy goes into a shadow index (<uid>__cdc_shadow_<time>) created with the live index's settings, which is swapped in when complete; search keeps using the old index meanwhile. Without it, the index is emptied first (in-place resync: clearing …) and fills up again. Refused for tasks in stream mode. Reset checkpoint moderator Forgets the sync progress; the next start runs a full snapshot. A running task restarts at once. Documents are not deleted first (unless zero-downtime resync rebuilds into a shadow index), so documents of rows deleted meanwhile can remain; prefer Resync to rebuild. Edit admin See Editing a task. Delete admin See Deleting a task. Actions are available on the task page, in the task list, to the API (POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/{action} with start, stop, pause, resume, restart, resync or reset-checkpoint) and to AI agents over MCP.

When the source can no longer resume from the stored position (purged binlog, dropped or invalidated replication slot, expired DynamoDB shard, oplog rolled over, trimmed Redis stream, SQL Server cleanup), the task logs source position lost (…); starting a full resync and resyncs by itself, honouring zero-downtime resync.

Edit opens the wizard with the current definition (admin). Masked secrets are kept unless you replace them. A running task restarts with the new definition. Changing the source (type, connector, table, schema or database) or the index (uid or destination) clears the checkpoint: the next start runs a full snapshot (source or index changed: checkpoint cleared, the next start runs a full snapshot). Changing managed settings of a stopped task applies them to the index right away; a running task applies them when it restarts. The id cannot change.

Deleting removes the definition, checkpoint, status, dead letters and diff report, and stops the task. The confirmation asks you to type the task id and offers two options: Drop source replication objects (checked by default; API dropSource=true): for PostgreSQL, drops the replication slot and the generated publication, so the database stops retaining WAL. Other sources keep nothing on the server that needs dropping; a Kafka consumer group is left in place. Also delete index (API deleteIndex=<uid>, which must equal the task's index uid): deletes the Meilisearch index and its documents. Otherwise documents stay.

Select tasks in the list to start, stop, pause, resume, restart, resync or delete them together (moderator; delete needs admin). Up to 8 tasks are processed in parallel and the result of each is reported. A batch delete never drops source objects nor deletes indexes. API: POST /api/v1/tasks/batch with {"ids": [...], "action": "resync"}.

Export (admin) downloads every task definition as JSON, with passwords and secret keys masked. Import (admin) creates the tasks of a JSON array, stopped. Tasks whose id exists, or that fail validation, are reported and skipped. Replace masked secrets, or use connectors, before importing into another installation. For tasks kept in Git, use the declarative tasks file instead.

A task page: counters, documents per second and lag over time, checkpoint and runtime details. Tab Contents Overview Counters (upserted, deleted, events, batches, errors, retries, dead letters, coalesced), rate and lag charts over the last ten minutes, snapshot progress, the checkpoint, in-flight batches, the last error. Webhook tasks also show the push endpoint. Logs The task's activity log (the last 1,000 entries, kept in memory), streamed live with auto-scroll. Schema check Source columns versus index fields and settings. See Data quality. Diff Document-level comparison with repair. See Diff and repair. DLQ Dead letters with replay and discard. See Dead letter queue. Index settings Desired versus live settings, drift and Apply. See Drift. Config The task definition as JSON (secrets masked), with links to edit it.

Lag is the time between a change's commit in the source and its confirmation in Meilisearch. When a streaming task is idle, its lag returns to zero. Rate is documents per second, smoothed. Last sync is when Meilisearch last confirmed a batch of the task.

Manage Meilisearch index settings from meilisearch-cdc: the settings editor, drift detection, primary keys, swap, compaction, search and documents. meilisearch-cdc manages the Meilisearch side too: index settings with drift detection, primary keys, swaps, compaction, a search playground and a documents browser, for every destination. Indexes grouped per instance, with the tasks that write to each.

All instances are queried in parallel and their indexes listed per instance (default first). An unreachable instance is shown with its error. Each index shows its primary key, document count, whether it is indexing, and the tasks that write to it. Actions (admin): Create index with a uid and an optional primary key. Usually unnecessary: tasks create their index on first write. Swap indexes: exchange the contents of two indexes atomically, or rename one to a new uid. Compact: ask Meilisearch to compact the index's storage. Delete: type the uid to confirm. Refused with 409 while a running task writes to the index; stop the task first.
Open an index for three tabs:

A playground for Meilisearch searches: query, filter expression, sort (field:asc or field:desc, comma separated), result limit, and the raw JSON response. Use it to check that a change in the source reached the index, or to try filters before building them into your application. The search playground.
Browse documents page by page and open any document as JSON.

The live settings in the settings editor. Changes are previewed (which keys change, from what to what) before they are applied; applying waits up to 30 seconds for Meilisearch and shows its error when it rejects the update. Reset restores Meilisearch's defaults. The primary key of an index can be changed here only while it holds no documents (409 otherwise).

The same editor is used in the task wizard (desired settings) and on index pages (live settings). It has a form view and a JSON view. Only the keys you set are sent; unset keys keep Meilisearch's defaults. Sections: The settings editor; a dot marks sections changed from the defaults. Filterable attributes can use Meilisearch's granular form (attribute patterns with per-pattern features such as facet search or equality-only filters). Field names discovered from the source are offered as suggestions. Ranking rules rankingRules The order of relevancy criteria (words, typo, proximity, attribute, sort, exactness) and custom rules such as price:asc. Words & tokens stopWords, dictionary, separatorTokens, nonSeparatorTokens Ignored words, custom dictionary entries and how text is split into words.
